scopeNote: Sequential phenotype/genetics, HCM, dilated and arrhythmogenic disease, restrictive/infiltrative disease, myocarditis/sarcoidosis and distinct acquired/pregnancy-related cardiomyopathies. Provisional coverage-driven decisions, not official exam weights.

sourceChecks.source: ESC cardiomyopathy guideline 2023
checked: NDLVC can include nonischemic scar without dilatation or reduced global EF.
Hypertrabeculation is a phenotypic trait, not automatically a separate cardiomyopathy.
Imaging pattern guides etiology but does not by itself establish gene or active inflammation.
Autosomal dominant transmission differs from age-dependent expression; VUS is not definitive predictive evidence.
A clinically normal relative negative for an established familial cause can usually leave surveillance directed at that cause.
Adult HCM threshold 15 mm; adult first-degree relative threshold 13 mm; LVOTO definition 30 mmHg differs from usual advanced-treatment threshold 50 mmHg.

sourceChecks.source: AHA/ACC HCM guideline 2024 and ESC myocarditis guideline 2025
checked: Current HCM advanced-treatment framework identified; symptom and gradient requirements must be separated from phenotype diagnosis.
Myocarditis imaging/biopsy guidance identified for detailed checks during later question batches.

sourceChecks.source: AHA/ACC HCM guideline 2024 official recommendation slide set
checked: Exercise echo for symptomatic patients without significant obstruction on initial maneuvers; CMR/contrast imaging for incompletely defined apical phenotype.
Integrated athlete differential rather than one thickness measurement.
Nonvasodilating beta blocker first-line, appropriate NDCC substitution, advanced options without mandatory disopyramide failure.
Phenylephrine or another noninotropic vasoconstrictor after fluid treatment in hypotension with dynamic obstruction.

sourceChecks.source: Mavacamten FDA label September 2026
checked: Interrupt below LVEF 50% even without overt symptoms; initiation/up-titration below 55% not recommended.
Adult usual initiation 5 mg/day and maximum 15 mg/day; interactions require separate dose pathways.
September 2026 indication includes pediatric weight >=30 kg, distinct from adult-only guideline-era wording; additive negative-inotrope and CYP restrictions reviewed.

sourceChecks.source: EXPLORER-HCM and SEQUOIA-HCM randomized evidence
checked: EXPLORER functional composite at 30 weeks, 37% vs 17%; not mortality or head-to-head surgery.
SEQUOIA peak oxygen uptake at 24 weeks; between-group 1.7 mL/kg/min, CI 1.0–2.4; no cross-trial superiority inference.

sourceChecks.source: AHA/ACC HCM guideline 2024 and ESC cardiomyopathy guideline 2023
checked: Myectomy when another cardiac lesion requires surgery; selection and limitations of alcohol ablation.
Adult major risk-marker definitions including aneurysm with scar, EF <50%, massive LVH and relevant family history; extensive LGE >=15% as additional evidence.
Separate adult risk-model bands and additional evidence rather than inventing a combined score.
HCM clinical-AF anticoagulation independent of conventional score; distinguish >24h from >5min to <24h subclinical episodes.
Systolic dysfunction threshold <50%; age-specific genotype-positive surveillance and sports counseling.

sourceChecks.source: ESC cardiomyopathy/myocarditis guidance and EHRA/ACNAP 2026
checked: CMR and cause-directed testing in stable unexplained DCM; biopsy is selected when it changes management, not mandatory before noninvasive characterization.
LMNA phenotype can begin with conduction and atrial disease before ventricular dysfunction; pacing alone does not settle ventricular-arrhythmia protection.

sourceChecks.source: Genetic alcohol-toxicity study 2018; DSP phenotype cohort 2020; ESC cardiomyopathy 2023
checked: Pathogenic TTN truncation and alcohol exposure may contribute together, without treating every TTN finding as pathogenic.
DSP phenotype can include recurrent myocardial injury and LV fibrosis before systolic dysfunction; not a universal indication for immunosuppression.

sourceChecks.source: Revised ARVC Task Force criteria 2010 and ESC 2023
checked: CMR regional finding plus sex-specific RVEDVi or EF threshold; a composite imaging criterion must not be counted twice.
Male major RVEDVi >=110; female >=100 mL/m2; major RVEF <=40%; minor volume/EF bands.
Age >14 and no complete RBBB for major V1–V3 T-wave inversion; distinct complete-RBBB context and terminal activation threshold >=55 ms.

sourceChecks.source: ESC 2023; HRS athlete-arrhythmia consensus 2024; ESC myocarditis 2025
checked: Sarcoidosis and loading/congenital disorders can mimic ARVC; consider directed inflammatory evaluation when the phenotype is discordant.
Intensive endurance exercise can accelerate ARVC phenotype/arrhythmia, particularly PKP2; ICD is not protection from substrate progression.
Arrhythmic history and both ventricular phenotypes remain relevant above conventional LV-EF primary-prevention thresholds.

sourceChecks.source: ESC cardiomyopathy and myocarditis/pericarditis guidance
checked: Respiratory ventricular discordance distinguishes constrictive physiology; pressure equalization and dip-and-plateau alone are not specific.

sourceChecks.source: ACC amyloidosis 2023, ATTR guidance 2025, ESC amyloid 2021 and ASH diagnostic guideline 2026
checked: Complete monoclonal screen uses serum free light chains plus serum/urine immunofixation; CKD interpretation matters.
Nonbiopsy ATTR requires phenotype plus grade 2/3 true myocardial uptake and negative complete clonal assessment; SPECT excludes blood-pool mimic.
Positive monoclonal result prevents automatic scan-based ATTR typing; tissue confirmation and validated fibril subtyping needed.
ASH 2026 supports appropriate combined surrogate or cardiac biopsy strategy; a negative surrogate sample does not end persistent suspicion.
Offer counseled TTR sequencing after ATTR regardless of older age or absent neuropathy/pedigree.

sourceChecks.source: Current ATTR drug labels and ACC ATTR guidance 2025
checked: TTR production silencing differs from tetramer stabilization; vutrisiran adult ATTR-CM indication includes wild-type and hereditary disease.
Adult labeled doses: vutrisiran 25 mg SC each 3 months; acoramidis 712 mg twice daily; tafamidis free acid 61 mg daily or meglumine 80 mg daily.
Vitamin A supplementation and lack of universal cross-trial ranking/combination mandate.

sourceChecks.source: ANDROMEDA original trial and final survival analysis 2026; daratumumab/hyaluronidase label
checked: Daratumumab-VCd in an eligible newly diagnosed AL population; do not extrapolate automatically to excluded Mayo stage IIIB.
Final analysis median follow-up 61.4 months, OS HR 0.62, CI 0.42–0.90.
Reference VCd doses and six-cycle duration verified in author manuscript; individualized dose reduction remains essential.

sourceChecks.source: Fabry GeneReviews and agalsidase/migalastat prescribing information
checked: Normal alpha-galactosidase A does not exclude Fabry in a woman; molecular testing and validated variant interpretation needed.
Agalsidase beta 1 mg/kg IV every two weeks; migalastat 123 mg every other day for eligible adults with amenable variants.

sourceChecks.source: TIF thalassemia guidance 2021/2025 and ESC eosinophilic-heart consensus 2026
checked: Validated cardiac T2* below ten milliseconds warrants urgent chelation review despite preserved EF; ferritin/liver iron cannot substitute for myocardial assessment.
Endocardial fibrosis, overlying thrombus and apical obliteration; eosinophilic inflammatory/thrombotic/fibrotic phases may overlap.
sourceChecks.accessNote: 2025 TIF chapter direct open hit browser challenge; accessible TIF 2021 guideline and 2022 TIF guide confirm numeric risk thresholds. No claim of full 2025 chapter access.

sourceChecks.source: ESC myocarditis/pericarditis 2025, ACC myocarditis pathway 2024 and updated CMR tissue recommendations 2018
checked: Exclude time-sensitive coronary disease rather than diagnosing myocarditis from a prodrome.
CMR T2 plus T1 tissue domains; functional/pericardial findings supportive, site-specific mapping values, timing and negative-test limitations.
Management-changing biopsy in high-risk HF/VT/AV-block phenotype; specialized processing and patchy-disease limitations.
Supportive/risk-based uncomplicated management rather than universal immunosuppression or serology-selected antiviral therapy.

sourceChecks.source: ISHLT/HFSA acute MCS guideline 2023 and ACC/ESC myocarditis guidance
checked: Early advanced-center escalation in refractory hypoperfusion; MCS as bridge to recovery/decision/transplant, with device selection by physiology and parallel tissue evaluation.

sourceChecks.source: TIMIC original randomized trial and current inflammatory cardiomyopathy guidance
checked: Selected chronic biopsy-proven virus-negative inflammatory cardiomyopathy; not all acute myocarditis.
Prednisone 1 mg/kg/day four weeks then 0.33 mg/kg/day five months and azathioprine 2 mg/kg/day six months, added to HF treatment.

sourceChecks.source: ESC myocarditis 2025 and eosinophilic-heart consensus 2026
checked: Giant-cell disease requires prompt combined immunosuppression rather than steroid monotherapy, with parallel HF/rhythm/transplant assessment.
ESC severe-disease pulse methylprednisolone dosing and subsequent oral steroid regimen; individualized additional agents and monitoring.
Drug-hypersensitivity myocarditis: culprit withdrawal plus systemic glucocorticoids for important myocardial involvement; assess alternative eosinophilic causes.
Fulminant eosinophilic pulse 7–14 mg/kg/day, max 1000 mg/day for three days; Strongyloides evaluation/treatment risk before or alongside urgent immunosuppression.

sourceChecks.source: ESC cardio-oncology 2022 and myocarditis 2025
checked: Preserved EF does not exclude serious ICI myocarditis with AV block; interrupt ICI and provide continuous monitored care.
Named ESC 2022 regimen methylprednisolone 500–1000 mg IV daily for first three to five days once likely; do not wait for biopsy in a high-risk likely presentation.
Reassess early for resistance; adjunct evidence/sequencing and rechallenge require multidisciplinary review.

sourceChecks.source: AHA cardiac sarcoidosis statement and ESC sarcoid consensus 2024
checked: CMR and adequately prepared PET are complementary; negative unguided biopsy does not exclude patchy disease; named clinical criteria matter.
US class IIa ICD assessment above EF 35% with permanent-pacing indication; distinguish device capability from CRT eligibility.
AHA prednisone initiation around 30–40 mg/day, individualized taper; ESC methotrexate 15–25 mg weekly with folic acid and monitoring.

sourceChecks.source: ESC myocarditis 2025, ACC pathway 2024 and international rhythm consensus 2026
checked: Individualized return after multiparametric remission; symptoms, troponin and EF alone do not override residual exercise-associated NSVT.
Persistent LGE is not synonymous with active inflammation or a universal permanent exercise ban.
Repeat CMR around six months and phase/substrate-directed rhythm evaluation contribute to follow-up.

sourceChecks.source: ESC pregnancy guideline 2025 and HFA PPCM consensus 2026
checked: PPCM EF <45%, peripartum timing and exclusion of adequate alternative cause; LV dilatation not required.
Pregnancy-compatible HF plan differs from postpartum/lactation plan; no antenatal ACEi/ARB/ARNI/MRA/SGLT2 default regimen.
ESC 2025 bromocriptine may-be-considered adjunct, at least prophylactic LMWH consideration, lactation implications and distinction between trial/acute dosing contexts.
Counsel recurrence even after EF >50%; consider continued HF therapy at least 12 months after complete recovery before individualized changes.

sourceChecks.source: InterTAK consensus 2018 and practical-challenges consensus 2024
checked: CAD and pheochromocytoma do not automatically exclude TTS; trigger not mandatory.
Do not delay urgent ACS work-up because ballooning is suspected.
Shock management depends on LVOTO/pump/RV/MR mechanism; do not increase inotropy indiscriminately in dynamic obstruction.

sourceChecks.source: ESC cardio-oncology 2022 and cardiomyopathy 2023; TTN alcohol-toxicity study
checked: Relative GLS magnitude reduction 20%; asymptomatic EF >=50 with >15% GLS decline meets mild CTRCD; moderate/severe EF bands remain distinct.
Address arrhythmia and alcohol exposure in parallel with HF treatment; reversible contributors do not exclude genetic susceptibility.

editorialReviewProgress.remaining: None for this chapter author-review gate; independent clinician review is not claimed.
changes: Q2 replaces unrelated cardiomyopathy labels with clinically plausible morphology, anticoagulation and family-testing interpretations.
Q3 now tests the actual LGE contrast principle against related CMR tissue mechanisms, retaining pattern and activity limitations in the explanation.
Q6 replaces prophylactic ICD/lifelong-health distractors with competing family surveillance and testing strategies.
Q8 replaces implausible gradient addition with competing resting, latent and nonobstructive classifications.
Q9 removes giveaway descriptions from competing investigation names.
Q11 replaces electrical monitoring and deliberately inadequate repeat views with competing cardiac imaging investigations.
Q12 compares actual obstructive-HCM treatment options under the explicitly dated 2024 pathway.
Q14 replaces waiting for EF decline with a plausible but unsuitable default dual-nodal drug escalation and shortens the correct option.
Q15 replaces disopyramide addition with a closer interruption-versus-permanent-discontinuation choice; adds distinct aficamten EF rules.
Q16 adds the separate MAPLE-HCM active-comparator trial and dose context without attributing it to the earlier placebo-controlled studies.
Q17 removes explicit left-untreated phrasing and compares surgical mitral/septal strategies rather than pacing as a weak substitute.
Q18 compares a major HCM marker with genuine additional/model risk features: extensive LGE, NSVT and LA size.
Q19 replaces invented percentage arithmetic with plausible competing ICD decisions: model-only exclusion, mandatory scar-driven implantation and EPS prerequisite.
Q22 replaces prophylactic ICD and unconditional discharge distractors with competing surveillance and preventive-drug plans.
Q23 presents realistic investigation names without universal/definitive giveaway qualifications.
Q27 now states definite, borderline and possible 2010 diagnostic combinations and explicitly avoids double-counting composite CMR evidence.
Q28 compares four closely competing major/minor and repolarization/depolarization categories rather than an unsupported definite-diagnosis claim.
Q29 replaces idiopathic focus/athlete/shunt distractors with giant-cell, lymphocytic and DSP-associated inflammatory disease.
Q30 replaces total inactivity and implausible ICD progression prevention with realistic competing exercise-clearance plans.
Full explanation review completed for questions 33-61, including diagnostic branches, drug schedules, activity assessment and pregnancy care.

Replaced weak or giveaway alternatives in amyloid, iron, inflammatory myocardial disease, device, PPCM and reversible-contributor questions with competing investigations, regimens or care sequences; individualized rationales revised to match.
Shortened long correct options in thirteen questions to reduce answer-length cueing.
Added primary ATTR-ACT, ATTRibute-CM and HELIOS-B trial comparisons to question 37, distinguishing hierarchical win ratios from mortality hazard ratios and avoiding cross-trial superiority claims.
Added migalastat renal eligibility and fasting/caffeine administration requirements from the 2025 US label.
Added an explicitly illustrative extended-release metoprolol starting dose with an ACC clinical teaching source; titration remains response- and tolerance-guided.
Applied numerical threshold and dose highlighting to teaching text and tables without changing stems or answer wording.

limitations: Author source checking does not constitute independent clinician review.
Structural validation is not proof of clinical accuracy or chapter completeness.

additionalSourceChecks.findings: Rechecked NDLVC and hypertrabeculation framework; extracellular gadolinium distribution differs from native T1/T2/T2-star mechanisms. Existing cascade-test and LVOT threshold source checks retained.

CMR clarification after inconclusive echo, physiological exercise echo and 2024 first-line/escalation pathways rechecked. Aficamten label has dose reduction at EF 40–<50 and interruption <40, unlike mavacamten. MAPLE is a separate 2025 active-comparator study; current evidence is not silently backdated into the 2024 guideline.

additionalSourceChecks.findings: Reviewed surgical selection, adult major-versus-additional risk features, risk-model interpretation, clinical-AF anticoagulation, HCM systolic impairment and genotype-positive surveillance. DCM investigation/LMNA explanation also read in full.
Read all explanations in full; reviewed sex-specific CMR and ECG conduction context, integrated diagnostic categories, inflammatory mimics, exercise exposure and ventricular interdependence.
